stories.h: Seattle mayor to announce CCTV camera plans after audit
stories.s: An NYU Policing Project audit of SPD's Real-Time Crime Center found policy gaps and made 19 recommendations. Mayor Katie Wilson announces next steps on the 62-camera program today at 11:15 a.m.

stories.h: Seattle schools authorize legal action over I-638 sports law
stories.s: The Seattle School Board voted Monday to hire counsel for possible legal action against voter-approved Initiative 638, which bars transgender girls from girls' teams. The law takes effect Dec. 3.

stories.h: Rain and gusty winds today; no river flooding expected
stories.s: Rain and 20-25 mph Puget Sound gusts arrive Tuesday, with possible record warmth Wednesday. NWS expects no river flooding this week; a stronger wind and rain system follows Friday.

stories.h: Nightly lane closures on I-90, I-5 and SR 167 this week
stories.s: WSDOT is closing eastbound I-90 lanes and ramps on Mercer Island nightly through Nov. 16. Up to three southbound I-5 lanes between Kent and Federal Way close overnight Thursday.

stories.h: Saturday windstorm cut power to tens of thousands
stories.s: Gusts near 50 mph knocked out power to more than 42,000 Seattle City Light customers overnight Saturday, with outages concentrated in South and West Seattle, Burien and White Center.

coming.h: Veterans Day: King County offices closed
coming.s: King County offices close Wednesday for Veterans Day, and some services run reduced schedules. Metro buses run weekday schedules. Normal operations resume Thursday.

coming.h: Stronger wind and rain system arrives Friday
coming.s: Forecasters expect a stronger storm Friday into the weekend, bringing more wind, rain and high-elevation snow. Strong winds could reach the Puget Sound interior.
